title: attention-kernel-optimization-profiling-comparative-notes
content:
Context:
Small working notes from profiling runs comparing FlashAttention, paged-KV approaches, and fused attention kernels. Goal: identify dominant bottlenecks on A100/H100, estimate token/s improvements, and surface actionable changes for the runtime (kernel selection heuristics, batching hints, and fallback policies).

Summary (top-line):
- FlashAttention gives the largest memory win and often the best throughput for medium->long sequences (seq_len >= 1024) when tensor cores are well-utilized.
- Paged-KV (KV paging) reduces peak memory and allows larger batch*seq runs but adds CPU/GPU synchronization overhead; beneficial for long-seq, small-batch interactive workloads.
- Fused ops (attention + qkv + softmax fused kernels) reduce kernel launch overhead and intermediate mem ops, improving p99 latency for small to medium sequences and improving single-stream perf.
- Combined approach: FlashAttention + fused kernels when possible; fall back to paged-KV variants when memory constrained.

Profiling setup and reproducibility notes:
- Hardware: NVIDIA A100 80GB (PCIe) and NVIDIA H100 SXM (80GB) nodes.
- Driver/CUDA: 535.86 / CUDA 12.2 for H100, 515.xx / CUDA 11.8 for A100 test matrix (kept historically consistent with infra images).
- Tools: Nsight Systems (ncu) for kernel timeline, Nsight Compute for per-kernel metrics, nvprof traces for quick checks, CUPTI counters for memory bandwidth sampling.
- Workloads tested: GPT-like decoder-only transformer with 8 heads, d_model=2048, rotary embeddings disabled (we used model config mirroring our production rtx-7b-2k).
- Input configs: batch sizes [1,4,8,32], seq lens [64,256,512,1024,2048], request patterns: single-request interactive (batch 1) and batched inference (batch up to 32).
- Measurement: steady-state token/s measured via synthetic feeder for 60s after a 10s warmup; latency p50/p95/p99 captured for interactive traces. Memory tracked via nvidia-smi sampling.

Important commands (examples):
- Nsight Systems trace: nsys profile --sample=cpu -o trace nsamples --trace=cuda ./run_inference --config=...
- Nsight Compute per-kernel: ncu --target-processes all --set full ./inference_binary ...
- Token/s harness: python perf_harness.py --model=... --bs=1 --seq=1024 --duration=60 --warmup=10

Key findings and metrics (representative):
- A100, batch=1, seq=1024:
  - Baseline (naive attention): 2.8k tokens/s, p99 latency 420ms
  - FlashAttention (patched runtime kernel): 6.7k tokens/s, p99 180ms, GPU mem peak -30%
  - Fused ops (qkv+attn softmax fused): 4.5k tokens/s, p99 240ms
  - Paged-KV enabled: 5.9k tokens/s, p99 210ms, host-GPU sync overhead visible in timeline (CPU stalls ~15ms every request)
- H100, batch=1, seq=1024:
  - FlashAttention: 9.1k tokens/s, p99 120ms (tensor core improvements + improved sm_efficiency)
  - Fused ops: 6.0k tokens/s, p99 170ms
- Batch=32, seq=256 (throughput mode):
  - Baseline: 18k tokens/s
  - FlashAttention: 36k tokens/s
  - Fused ops: 32k tokens/s
  - Paged-KV: not needed for short seq; incurs overhead and falls behind by ~10%

Bottleneck analysis (kernel-level):
- Memory bandwidth and DRAM writes: naive implementations suffer large intermediate writes for attention score matrices; FlashAttention reduces these substantially by re-ordering computation and limiting high-precision temporaries.
- Kernel launch overhead: small-seq, single-request scenarios dominated by hundreds of microkernel launches; fused ops reduce number of launches and amortize overhead.
- Tensor core utilization: H100 shows higher win from FlashAttention because the algorithm maps favorable GEMM shapes to tensor cores; on A100 the benefit is present but smaller.
- L2 cache / shared memory thrashing: paged-KV variants cause more random accesses to past KV pages; if access pattern crosses page boundaries frequently we see increased L2 misses and degraded perf.
- CPU-GPU synchronization: paged-KV implementations that rely on host orchestration show CPU stalls visible in Nsight timeline; offloading more page management to GPU or using async prefetch improves steady-state.

Micro-optimizations worth experimenting with in runtime:
- Kernel selection policy: heuristics based on (batch, seq_len, model_dim) to prefer fused small-seq kernels, FlashAttention for medium/long seq, paged-KV for extreme seq when mem > threshold.
- Prefetching for paged-KV: async prefetch of next KV pages using CUDA IPC/streams to hide latency; maintain a small LRU on GPU for hottest pages.
- Batch reshaping: for mixed-size requests, pack small requests into a batch-friendly layout that aligns GEMM shapes for tensor cores; reduces kernel variance.
- Quantization + FlashAttention: verify correctness and perf when running 8-bit kernels; may need different kernel codepaths to avoid accuracy regressions.
- Reduce host-to-device synchronization by collapsing CPU-side control loops into a single orchestrator kernel where possible.

Risks, correctness checks, and edge cases:
- Numerical stability: FlashAttention recomputes softmax differently; verify extreme logit values and compare against stable baseline on a large eval set.
- Reproducibility across CUDA/driver versions: some kernels show divergent perf on newer drivers; pin test images or add CI single-run checks for perf regressions.
- Memory accounting: paged-KV reduces peak but increases meta-data; ensure OOM handling and correct fallbacks when page miss rate spikes.

Actionable recommendations (short-term):
1) Add a kernel-selection matrix in runtime config: default to fused small-seq, FlashAttention for seq>=512 (configurable threshold), and paged-KV only when GPU free mem < X% or seq > 2048.
2) Implement an async prefetch prototype for paged-KV with a small in-GPU LRU; measure CPU stalls reduction.
3) Add Nsight Compute perf tests in CI for representative kernels on available infra images (A100/H100). Fail on >10% regression vs baseline.
4) Add a correctness test suite comparing FlashAttention outputs vs reference softmax attention on 10k random sequences (monitor max abs diff and average KL).

Open questions / next experiments:
- How does FlashAttention interact with rotary embeddings or ALiBi? Need targeted tests because positional modifications affect kernel memory access patterns.
- Evaluate hybrid approach: use FlashAttention for most layers, paged-KV for top N layers where history is large. Does this balance memory and perf?
- GPU multi-tenant behavior: when collocated workloads reduce available memory, how often should runtime switch to paged-KV? Build a threshold-decider based on live mem pressure signals.

Appendix (notes from timeline traces):
- Example trace snippet (batch=1, seq=1024): CPU dispatch -> qkv GEMM (50ms) -> FlashAttention kernel run (70ms) -> output post-processing (10ms). No intermediate large memcpy noted.
- Paged-KV trace shows repeated small memcpy H2D for page misses (8-12ms spikes) and small kernel runs for page management.

References and links:
- FlashAttention paper and upstream impl notes (linked in Confluence).
- Internal PR: github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/412 contains prototype kernels and benchmark harness.

Notes to self / TODOs:
- Run longer-duration stability tests (24h) on H100 to check thermal throttling effects on p99.
- Add more granularity for seq in [1536,1792] where we saw non-linear perf cliffs.
- Coordinate with infra to run same suite on a A100 multi-instance GPU (MIG-like split) to see multi-tenant effects.

-- end of notes --
